note: Original IELTS-format practice material (not official IELTS content). Part 1: short linked interview questions on a familiar topic. Part 2: cue card (task, cue points, 'and explain' line). Part 3: abstract discussion linked to the theme of a Part 2 card.

part1.title: Your hometown
q: Where is your hometown?
What do you like most about it?
Is it a good place for young people to live? Why?
How has your hometown changed in recent years?

part1.title: Your home
q: Do you live in a house or an apartment?
Which room do you spend the most time in?
What would you like to change about your home?
Do you plan to live there for a long time?

part1.title: Work or studies
q: Do you work or are you a student?
What do you enjoy most about your work or studies?
Is there anything you find difficult about it?
What would you like to do in the future?

part1.title: Mornings

part1.title: Weekends
q: What do you usually do at weekends?

part1.title: Friends
q: Do you have a lot of friends?
How often do you see your friends?
What do you like doing together?

part1.title: Neighbours

part1.title: Plants and flowers

part1.title: Music

part1.title: Reading

part1.title: Photographs

What do you usually take photos of?

Do you ever draw or paint now?

part1.title: Handwriting

part1.title: Holidays

part1.title: Walking

part1.title: Birthdays

part1.title: Gifts

What kind of gifts do you like to receive?
Do you prefer a gift or money?

part1.title: Festivals

What do people do during that festival?
Do you enjoy festivals?

part1.title: Museums

When was the last time you went to one?

part1.title: History

Are you interested in the history of your town?
How do you usually learn about history?

part1.title: Learning languages

part1.title: Science

part1.title: Childhood

What did you like to do as a child?

part1.title: Noise
q: Is the place where you live noisy or quiet?
What kinds of noise do you find annoying?
Can you work or study in a noisy place?

part1.title: Parks

part1.title: Being on time

part1.title: Relaxing
q: How do you usually relax?
Do you find it easy to relax?
Is it better to relax alone or with friends?

part3.title: Teachers and teaching
q: What qualities make someone a good teacher?
Is teaching a more difficult job now than it was in the past?
Should teachers be paid more? Why or why not?
Can technology ever replace teachers?
Why do some people choose teaching as a career?

part3.title: Helping others
q: Why do some people enjoy helping others more than others do?
Do people help strangers less than they used to?
Should children be taught to help others at school?
Is it better to help people with money or with time?

part3.title: Older people in society
q: What can young people learn from older people?
How has the role of grandparents changed in modern families?
Should older people continue working if they want to?
What can society do to make sure older people are not lonely?

part3.title: Friendship
q: Why do some friendships last longer than others?
Is it easier to make friends as a child or as an adult?
Can online friends be as close as friends you meet in person?
How important is it to have friends with different opinions from yours?

part3.title: Creativity
q: Are people born creative, or can creativity be taught?
Do schools do enough to develop children's creativity?
In which jobs is creativity most important?
Is creativity more valued today than it was in the past?

part3.title: Sport and role models
q: Are famous athletes good role models for young people?
Why are top athletes paid so much?

How does watching sport influence people's own activity levels?

part3.title: Quiet and noise
q: Why do people need quiet places in their lives?

How does noise affect people's health and work?
Should there be stricter rules about noise in residential areas?

part3.title: Tourism
q: What are the benefits of tourism for a city?

How has the way people choose holiday destinations changed?
Should popular cities limit the number of tourists?

part3.title: Architecture

part3.title: Protecting nature
q: Why is it important to protect natural areas?

part3.title: Public spaces

How have people's uses of public spaces changed in recent years?

Is it better to buy cheap things often or expensive things that last?
